text:
sasha: 09:12 UTC — p99 for /generate on g5x-small pool jumped from ~220ms to ~1.1s. Affects ~12% of traffic. Noticed right after the morning canary push.
raj: also seeing it. Can confirm spike aligns with infra driver/tensor runtime push at ~08:50. Only hosts with Triton 2.10-ish and new kernel-selector heuristic.
perf-bot: quick profile (08:50-09:15, sample pool=g5x-small):
```
$ triton-kernel-stats --since 08:45 --pool g5x-small
GEMM_FP16      78.2%
flash_attn_fwd  5.1%  (was ~62% before)
other          16.7%
```
kevin: that shift is huge. looks like selector stopped preferring flash_attn for short-seq cases — but our batching combinator is coalescing lots of short requests into wide batches which then steer it to GEMM path. With KV-hit heavy workloads GEMM is suboptimal (more memory ops).
nicole: i reproduced locally with a 70% KV-reuse synthetic workload + burst of short prompts. Kernel selector chose GEMM for many steps. Quick hack: forcing flash_attn preference for seq<=32 in selector brought p99 back down to ~240ms in the sim.
raj: possible root cause: the new heuristic used 90th percentile sequence length of the *raw* batch before prefix/KV folding, so when many tiny sequences are merged we see inflated seq stats and choose GEMM. need to incorporate KV-hit ratio and effective decoded steps.
infra-bot: rolled partial revert: triton runtime rolled back to 2.9 on 3 canary hosts, driver pinned to 535.80 at 09:40.
sasha: after revert, p99 on those canaries dropped to ~260ms (from 1.1s). Slowly rolling the revert to remainder of g5x-small pool; monitoring dashboards show improvement.
raj: action items: 1) Add KV-hit-aware check to kernel selector heuristic (PR in flight #4210). 2) Expose emergency runtime flag REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE_FLASH_SHORTSEQ for ops to toggle quickly. 3) Add alert that triggers when flash_attn share drops >30pp in 5m window. I'll file infra/rt-runtime tickets.
kevin: also adding a simulation test that reproduces mixed-batch KV-heavy workload to prevent regressions. Will add to eng-ml CI.
nicole: small follow-up: logging patch to emit "effective_seq" and "kv_hit_ratio" in trace samples so we can monitor selector inputs. Rolling that now.
sasha: great. marking incident as resolved -> monitoring. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
